title: OpenScreening
synopsis:
ATA’s free community film/video show welcomes short format work or (15 min or less) from all genres. An open forum for independent filmmakers to show their work, we hold screenings the first Thursday of the month at 8:00 pm. Entries must be received by 7:00 pm on show night.
Submissions: To submit a digital file, email openscreening@atasite.org. For physical media, label all tapes with name, contact info, title, and length, and mail to: Open Screening, 992 Valencia St, San Francisco, CA 94110. 1–2 weeks advance submissions recommended. If not, just walk in before the show.
Maximum length: 15 min.
Formats: Digital file (PC or Mac), DVD, miniDV/DV-cam, VHS, beta, 8 mm, and 16 mm. For 8 mm and 16 mm films give us advance notice.
Doors at 7:30 pm, show at 8:00 pm, FREE

title: Other Cinema: Incredibly Strange Religion
synopsis:
O My Gawd!! OC’s FALL CHARM BRACELET takes a skeptical bow towards alt-religion, art-religion, and fantasy cults with our annual Incredibly Strange Religion revival!! In tonight’s celebration of new, creative ritual imagination and performance, an apocalyptic 99 minutes of spiritual absurdity serves to support the all-too-rare return of the truly awesome Church of Magic, a tour de force performance-art initiative by ATA soulmate Ben Folstein!! After Cinema Studies under GeneYoungblood, the prodigiously talented Folstein dares to deliver his utterly INSANE appeal to celestial communion, with costumes, comic gestures, cosmic jokes, and a jubilant revival of his past music-video hits Zog, the First Feminist, Below Decks, Rock Too Big, and so much more! Opening this religious riot is a litany of jaw-dropping proposals by the now-legendary freak-belief sources Unarius, the Mormons (in Guatemala!), Christian Scientists, Scientologists, Church of Satan, etc. Sacred wine is free!
See the rest of Fall Season here.

title: CROSSROADS 2026 program 4: bury it in the garden
synopsis:
A community partnership with San Francisco Cinematheque
As a centerpiece, Maryam Tafakory’s Daria’s Night Flowers—“draw[ing] upon dozens of Persian-language films, both classics and obscurities, to weave a tale of jealousy, muted ambition, and creative suppression” (Michael Sicinski)—grounds a program of quiet incantations, rituals of remembrance, intergenerational traumas and healings and domestic anxieties. Works exploring mysteries within the everyday, losses latent in quotidian spaces.
SCREENING:
of the sun, that it exists (du soleil, que ça existe) (2025) by Charlotte Clermont (Canada); digital video, b&w, sound, 9 minutes. Exhibition file from AV-arkki. Jones Street (2025) by Silvia Turchin (US); digital video, color, sound, 11 minutes. In the Heavenly Cutting Room (2025) by Emma Penaz Eisner (US); digital video, color, sound, 3 minutes. Wildflower Season (2025) by Kathleen Quillian (US); digital video, color, sound, 8 minutes. گل‌های شب ِدریا Daria’s Night Flowers (2025) by Maryam Tafakory (Iran); digital video, color, sound, 16 minutes. Exhibition file from Square Eyes Film. (for once I dreamed of you) (2025) by Kate Solar (Canada); digital video, b&w, sound, 6 minutes. Exhibition file from Winnipeg Film Group. I Was There (2025) by Kamila Kuc (USA/Poland); digital video, color, sound, 13 minutes. 
TRT: 66 minutes

FESTIVAL PASSES: $85 General/$70 Cinematheque Members, Gray Area Members & students (with ID)

title: TINAFF
synopsis: This is Not a Film Festival (also know as TINAFF) is a monthly recurring film showcase, allowing local Bay Area filmmakers, artists and creatives to gather, connect, and present their work. No submission fees, no awards, no gatekeeping. Our goal is to provide a space where truly independent films can be shared and enjoyed the way they’re meant to be; with a live audience.

title: Rewards Program
synopsis:
A live-scored three-projector celluloid meditation with:

MILES LASSI is an interdisciplinary artist based out of Oakland, CA. As a musician, he has performed in over 150 cities throughout North America, Europe and Asia with many different ensembles ranging from the Vietnam National Symphony Orchestra at Carnegie Hall to national broadway tours like Ain’t Too Proud, Dirty Dancing, and Tina: The Tina Turner Musical. Miles is dedicated to creating new media and has done so at the New York Film Festival, Lincoln Center, Apollo Theater, deYoung Museum, Joyce Theater, Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture, A.C.T., SXSW and Snap Studios/KQED.



SKYWAY MAN is the alias of keyboardist, songwriter, and producer James Wallace. Based in Oakland via Richmond, VA, and Nashville, TN, he has released seven albums and composed music for Film/TV, including Joe Pera Talks With You (HBO). Over the past 15 years, he has toured extensively across the U.S., Europe, and Asia, performing at festivals like Bonnaroo, Pickathon, SXSW, Hardly Strictly Bluegrass, and Wilco’s Solid Sound. He has collaborated with Abigail Washburn, Langhorne Slim, Erin Rae, and Maya Hawke, among others. Brittany Howard once named his band a favorite local act in Rolling Stone, and his work has been featured in NPR, The Wall Street Journal, and Stereogum. He’s produced 20 full-length albums for other artists, including Bay Area musicians Mikayla McVey, Milk for the Angry, and Pancho Morris. Over the past few years he’s developed a practice of live instrumental film scoring using keyboards and sequencers.

ZEKARIAS MUSELE THOMPSON (b. 1983, they/them/their) is an artist based in Oakland, CA, and Reykjavik, IS often working in sonic composition, mark-making, photography, collaborative group practice & performance, and writing. Their practice is concerned with humanity’s conceptual and emotional organizational structures—and how we bring them into material form. Zekarias has presented solo exhibitions and projects at the Museum of the African Diaspora, the Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive, The Lab, Gray Area, the Santa Cruz Museum of Art and History, and the Center for New Music and Audio Technologies. Zekarias is a co-founder of Working Name Studios, a collectively owned and organized arts institution with the mission of building institutional stability and equity for underrepresented creative practices, ideas, and people. They were part of the Emerging Artist Program at the MoAD for 2024, and are currently an MFA candidate in the Department of Art Practice at UC Berkeley.


ELLIE VANDERLIP is a San Francisco-based experimental filmmaker, performer, and educator. She received her MFA in Cinema from San Francisco State University in 2022. She is a co-director at Oakland’s Shapeshifters Cinema, on the board of directors at San Francisco’s Cinematheque, and maintains a studio at Artists’ Television Access. She has hosted filmmaking workshops with the Exploratorium, Yerba Buena Center for the Arts, and the University of San Francisco, and lectures at St. Mary’s College and San Francisco State University. Her primary focuses are found footage experimental documentary, material cinema, and expanded cinema performance. Her work has screened nationally and internationally, including at San Francisco DocFest and Belgrade’s Kinoscope Festival, and has upcoming writings about alternative archives in Found Footage Magazine.

title: Other Cinema: Psychedelic Cinema
synopsis: OC is truly honored to welcome back esteemed European critic, author, and curator KorneliaBoczkowska! This incendiary cinema visionary is in fact a huge fan of West Coast aesthetics, and she keeps breaking new discursive ground around those idiosyncratic sensibilities that are so dear to our native filmmaking themes and practices. Tonight she unveils the regional premiere of an absolutely reality-ripping line-up of films that address…the Psychedelic State-of-Mind!! Among the genius heads on exhibition are Jordan Belson, Melissa Faivre, Linda Scobie, Dominic Angerame, Richard Tuohy/Dianna Barrie, and the world debut of Toney Merritt‘s Vision Quest Remix. These makers–and a dozen more!–attempt to induce hallucinatory states thru mesmerizing kaleidoscopic forms, pulsating lights, vivid colors, otherworldly sounds, and atmospheric imagery. Local superstars Scobie, Merritt, and Angerame materialize in person to share their brain-wave secrets! PLUS Glen McKay‘s Playland visuals, and, yes, Daisy Ascencio‘s liquid lightshow, out of our gallery’s much-revered overhead projector. $15

title: Other Cinema: Post-Kolonial Spectres
synopsis: A true breakthrough and international discovery!! Here in-person with A Human Year Is Seven Earth Years, Honduran-American Adrian Quetzal Randall has cooked up an unprecedented Meso-American mystery play, an extremely sophisticated personal cine-essay that opens up areas of speculative history in an Adam Curtis-esque stream-of-consciousness  revelation on the military origins of Central American telecommunications and programming, tracing a psychedelic labyrinth across four continents. Part media archeology, part film diary, an endless montage of archival opticals support a long-form whispered confession about the electromagnetic magick that inflected the development of “modern” Honduran national sensibility. Our co-hit is Riar Rizaldi‘s equally paranoid Tellurian Drama, a sublime 25-min excavation of the colonial mythos surrounding the infamous Malabar Radio Antenna, a mysterious site of etheric conspiracy now being resurrected as a tourist destination on the Indonesian island of Java. $13

title: Mālama Mākua
synopsis:
Nestled on the far West Side of O’ahu, Hawai’i, Mākua is a sacred valley where Native Hawaiian creation stories tell of earth and sky deities giving birth to the first people. Once a thriving community rich in natural abundance, Mākua’s was taken by the U.S. Army, which forcibly evicted its residents. For decades, the valley and its pristine beach were subjected to relentless military bombing and live-fire training, scarring both land and spirit in the name of national security. Mālama Mākua tells the story of a community that banded together to end the Military destruction of Mākua. A film 30 years in the making, Mālama Mākua chronicles the ongoing struggle to restore U.S. Military-occupied lands to Native Hawaiian stewardship.
Winner of the Audience Choice Award at the Hawai’i International Film Festival, Mālama Mākua traces the valley’s transformation from a place of deep cultural roots to a rallying point for grassroots activism. Connecting this local struggle to global movements for Indigenous sovereignty, demilitarization, and environmental justice, the film follows the people of Mākua as they fight to reclaim their ancestral lands. With the U.S. Army’s leases on the lands set to expire in 2029, the call for Mākua’s return grows more urgent than ever.

title: TINAFF: Program 7
synopsis:
This is Not a Film Festival (also know as TINAFF) is a monthly recurring film showcase, allowing local Bay Area filmmakers, artists and creatives to gather, connect, and present their work. No submission fees, no awards, no gatekeeping. Our goal is to provide a space where truly independent films can be shared and enjoyed the way they’re meant to be; with a live audience.
Rodney Rideout (15:23), Dir. Josh Blodget
When a civilian gets caught trespassing onto a crashlanded UFO, he has to kill all of the feds to make it out alive. 1970s grindhouse inspired action movie with practical stunts set to music.
Mask Up (2:22), Dir. Ryan Duncan
Two brothers must decide if an unlikely problem is going to stop them from robbing a liquor store.
Tuolumne (11:54), Dir. Riley Vitale
A young woman returns home after the passing of her sister.
Couch Ghosts (5:09), Dir. Jiaxin Zheng
Two college roommates bring home a pristine, free couch that seems too good to be true.
Crossing the Blue Line (14:33), Dir. Maricar Bella
Bound by their father’s toxic ambition, a rigid older brother confronts his hockey-prodigy sibling over his decision to quit the sport—sparking a volatile face-off to finally dismantle the generational trauma that tore their family apart.
Burrito Death Squad (13:52), Dir. Otto
When his bummy unemployed roommate finances too many burritos in his name, Will is forced to reconcile the obnoxiously large debt with a Death Squad.
~Intermission~ (15:00)
In the Meantime (14:52), Dir. Itai Rinat
In the aftermath of a tragic accident, a young photographer lives vicarious fantasies through his camera lens as he tracks down a woman in San Francisco who a mysterious craigslist poster claims to be his wife, culminating in a midnight confrontation at a karaoke bar.
ANTI CELL (5:18), Dir. Fabrice Ducouret
You’re breaking up
SavePoint (7:09), Dir. Sam Amaya
Upon reaching a mysterious portal in the woods, Theseus finds himself in the middle of a dilemma.
CASSEROLE (6:11), Dir. Pharoah T.K.E Harrington
A young couple are thrown into chaos when a burglary forces the young man to fight for their household.
Ciudad de México en Super 8 (4:13), Dir. Miles Moreira
Girls Gotta Eat (8:23), Dir. Micah Ochs
A hungry lesbian creature refuses to bring harm upon women despite being repulsed by men.
Eternidad (14:09), Dir. Iggy Munoz
A couple reunites in the afterlife.
